fixes.explanation: That's the offer, baker. The LORD says, “If you can find a single person, anyone who acts justly, anyone who seeks the truth, then I will forgive the city.” Notice who gets the benefit: the whole city, not just the one person who gets found. One person like that on the streets, and Jerusalem is forgiven. That's a door left wide open.
I like the thinking, but the verse never hands out a promotion. No robe, no gavel, no office. The LORD says, “…then I will forgive the city.” The reward named here is forgiveness for the whole city.

Nobody's calling a construction crew in this verse. The LORD's promise is, “…then I will forgive the city.” Forgiveness is what's on the table, not bricks and mortar. Walls just aren't part of this offer.

I see why you'd lean that way, baker. The speaker said, “Surely they know the way of the LORD…” Then the text says, “But they too, with one accord, had broken the yoke and torn off the chains.” So the powerful don't keep the way of the LORD. They did the very opposite.

Yes. Verse 6 says why: “For their rebellious acts are many, and their unfaithful deeds are numerous.” A lion, a wolf and a leopard are a heavy picture, and I think this part of the passage is a hard one. The text gives the reason plainly, and it's what the people have done.

That's the reason, baker, and it's the only one the LORD gives. He says, “Strip off her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.” Not too wild, not out of fruit. Just not His. When the text hands you the reason that plainly, I'm happy to leave it right there.

That's what they say. Verse 12 says they lied about the LORD and said, “He will not do anything; harm will not come to us; we will not see sword or famine.” The text calls it a lie, and it reports it as their words.

I see why you'd lean that way, but the text goes the other direction. In verse 13 the people say, “The prophets are but wind, for the word is not in them.” What they say is that the word isn't in the prophets.

Right. The people say, “The prophets are but wind, for the word is not in them.” That's the opposite of saying the prophets carry the LORD's word. They also say, “So let their own predictions befall them.”

Flood sounds like a believable pick, but it's not the word. The LORD says, “…I will make My words a fire in your mouth and this people the wood it consumes.” Fire is what He names, and He calls this people the wood.

The verse doesn't say its army will be small. It calls this nation distant, established and ancient, and says it's “…a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you do not understand.” Verse 16 also says of them, “they are all mighty men.”

Prophets did come up earlier, in verse 13, when the people called them wind. But the LORD's answer in verse 19 doesn't use them in either blank. He says they “…served foreign gods in your land, so will you serve foreigners in a land that is not your own.” The words that fit are gods and foreigners.
